messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT (P1) — tenant=stella, region=eu-west, symptom=high-queue-depth on dedicated pool, pages issued to #incidents  
infra-bot: Alert details: pool=dedicated-stella-eu-west-1, util=95%, queue_depth=3200, 5xx_rate=0.8%  
Alice M.: I'm on it, grabbing logs and verifying warm pool state. @Ben C. can you check warm capacity availability in eu-west?  
Ben C.: checking now — reserved warm nodes show 6 available, 2 warm images pending. ETA ~7m to spin to service.  
Jamie P.: what's customer impact? any 503s reported from Stella?  
Lucas (CSM): Stella reported increased latencies and some 502s from gateway, engineering team is standing by. They asked for a maintenance-aware cutover if possible.  
Ravi K.: can we do a gradual traffic shift instead of immediate DNS swap? prefer route-level shift to avoid long DNS TTL issues.  
Alice M.: agreed. Plan proposal: 1) provision warm pool (Ben) 2) enable overlay routing to warm pool and shift 10% traffic for canary 3) monitor error rates/latency 4) escalate to 100% cutover and then do DNS TTL update if needed.  
Maya P.: add automatic fallback: if 5xx > 1.5% for 3m, rollback to primary. I'll create the alert rule.  
Ben C.: warm pool provision started: rwctl infra warm-provision --tenant stella --region eu-west --nodes 6  
Ben C.: logs: "provisioning node stella-eu-03... init containers done"  
Alice M.: ETA for route config change once warm nodes are healthy: ~3m after provisioning.  
infra-bot: Healthcheck snapshot: 2/6 warm nodes ready, avg boot time 90s  
Ravi K.: prepping route command: 
```
rwctl route shift --tenant=stella --from=eu-west-primary --to=eu-west-warm --percent=10 --strategy=sticky-sessions
```  
Alice M.: good. set sticky-sessions=true to keep active sessions on origin. Stella uses short-lived sessions but we still want consistency.  
Jamie P.: I'm ready to watch logs + traces. @Maya P. can you wire the canary dashboard (latency, 5xx, queue_depth) to the incident channel?  
Maya P.: on it — dashboard link: https://console.redwood/shifts/1873456789/canary  
Lucas (CSM): I'll inform Stella SRE that we're starting a 10% canary and will confirm within 5 minutes.  
Alice M.: executing route shift now.  
infra-bot: COMMAND executed by Alice M.: rwctl route shift --tenant=stella --from=eu-west-primary --to=eu-west-warm --percent=10 --strategy=sticky-sessions  
incident-bot: ACTION — route-shift started, correlation_id=ci-1873456789-01  
Jamie P.: canary traffic live. tailing logs: `tail -f /var/log/routing/stella-eu-west.log` shows initial success lines.  
Ravi K.: monitoring traces: p90 latency for canary 120ms, p90 primary 240ms — looks good so far.  
Maya P.: alert rule check: 5xx 0.6% on canary, queue_depth down 12% overall.  
Lucas (CSM): Stella reports improved response times for the test requests. They want final cutover after 15m of stability.  
Alice M.: agree. Next step: ramp to 50% in 5m increments if stable. I'll schedule increments: 10% -> 30% -> 50% -> 100% if no regressions.  
Ben C.: warm pool now at 6/6 nodes ready.  
infra-bot: Healthcheck: all warm nodes passed readiness probes, cpu avg=18%  
Ravi K.: initiating ramp to 30%  
incident-bot: ACTION — route-shift update, correlation_id=ci-1873456789-02, percent=30  
Maya P.: canary dashboard stable for 8m, 5xx=0.7%, p95 latency improving.  
Jamie P.: logs look clean, small number of 502s on primary but trending down.  
Lucas (CSM): Stella approves continue. They asked whether we can shorten DNS TTL after cutover to avoid stale caches.  
Alice M.: yes — after we reach 100% and confirm, we'll set TTL to 60s for 1h window and then restore to 300s.  
Ravi K.: ramp to 50% now.  
incident-bot: ACTION — route-shift update, correlation_id=ci-1873456789-03, percent=50  
Maya P.: still stable. setting rollback watchdog: if 5xx > 1% for 3 consecutive minutes, auto-rollback to previous percent.  
Ben C.: preparing DNS change docs: target CNAME -> stella-eu-west.warm.redwood.net. TTL plan included.  
Alice M.: proceed to 100% if 15m at 50% looks clean.  
infra-bot: Observability snapshot: overall queue_depth halved, 5xx at 0.5% system-wide.  
Jamie P.: no new error spikes. ready for final step.  
Alice M.: executing final ramp to 100% and queue drain.  
incident-bot: ACTION — route-shift update, correlation_id=ci-1873456789-04, percent=100  
Maya P.: rolling window check starting — 15m stability timer engaged.  
Lucas (CSM): notifying Stella that Redwood is doing a full route cutover and will perform DNS TTL change after validation.  
Ravi K.: post-cutover: initiating DNS TTL drop: `dig +short stella.api.eu | xargs -I{} rwctl dns update --name stella.api.eu --cname stella-eu-west.warm.redwood.net --ttl 60`  
Ben C.: DNS update propagated to authoritative, next-hop CNAME set.  
infra-bot: DNS propagation sample: 8/10 resolvers seeing new CNAME within 120s.  
Jamie P.: no errors, logs show steady low latency.  
Alice M.: starting 15m validation window.  
Maya P.: validation passed at +15m — 5xx=0.4%, p95 latency improved 30%.  
Lucas (CSM): Stella confirms they see normal behavior from their end. they said thank you for the fast response. :tada:  
Alice M.: rolling TTL back to 300s in 30m after confirming stability window.  
incident-bot: RESOLVED — incident P1 (tenant=stella) mitigated via route-level warm pool cutover and DNS CNAME swap, postmortem assigned to Jamie P. and Ben C.  
Jamie P.: I'll take postmortem. notes: investigate root cause of primary pool queue growth and examine autoscaler tuning for tenant-specific bursts.  
Ben C.: will add warm-image init time optimization as action item.  
Maya P.: updating incident ticket with timelines and dashboards.  
Alice M.: thanks team — good run. closing thread in 10m unless any followups.  
Lucas (CSM): sharing a quick recap to Stella leadership now.  
incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (auto) in 10m if no activity."
